blocks.heading: Staking instead
text: On 15 September 2022 Ethereum stopped mining. Not gradually - between one block and the next.
The chain kept running, and its electricity bill fell by about 99.95%.

blocks.heading: Keep the problem, change the scarce thing
text: The requirement from lesson 13 has not moved: votes must cost something, or identities are free and the vote means nothing.
Work makes a vote cost electricity. Stake makes it cost **capital you have already handed over**.

blocks.heading: What a validator is
text: Someone who has deposited 32 ETH into a contract and runs software that proposes and attests to blocks.
The deposit is not a fee. It sits there, and the protocol can take it.

blocks.heading: The clock is fixed, not lottery-driven

blocks.alt: Three stacked steps: a 12-second slot, a 32-slot epoch of 6.4 minutes, and finality two epochs later at 12.8 minutes
blocks.caption: No memoryless search. A validator is chosen for each 12-second slot and simply proposes.

blocks.heading: Which lets it say a word bitcoin cannot
text: After two epochs, about 12.8 minutes, a block is **finalised**.
Not "very probably safe". Reverting it requires at least a third of all staked ETH to be destroyed by the protocol itself.

blocks.title: A price, not a probability
text: Lesson 16 gave Nora a curve that approaches zero and never arrives. Casper FFG gives a number instead: the attacker's own capital, forfeited.
That is a genuinely different kind of guarantee, and it is the strongest argument for the design.

blocks.question: Under proof of work, mining two competing chains splits your hashrate. Under staking, signing both costs nothing. What stops a validator voting for everything?
answer: Slashing. Proposing two blocks for one slot, or casting contradictory attestations, is provable from the signatures alone - the evidence is the validator's own signature, submitted by anyone who sees both.
The protocol then destroys part of the stake and ejects the validator. "Nothing at stake" is not solved by physics here; it is solved by writing down a punishment and making the proof self-contained.

blocks.heading: The switch itself was unusual
text: It was not scheduled at a block height or a date. It triggered at a **terminal total difficulty** - a cumulative amount of work.
The last mined block was the one that pushed the total past the threshold. After it, the beacon chain took over.

blocks.heading: And now the cost nobody advertises
text: Under proof of work, a brand-new node can verify everything from the genesis block using only the rules. Work is checkable from outside; the heaviest chain identifies itself.
Under proof of stake, validators who have withdrawn their deposits can sign an alternative history for free. There is nothing left to slash.

blocks.title: Weak subjectivity
text: So a node syncing from scratch cannot tell the real history from a fabricated one. It needs a recent block hash obtained out of band - from a friend, a client's defaults, a block explorer - and has to trust it.
It is a small, bounded, well-understood amount of trust. It is not zero, and proof of work needed none.

blocks.caption: Neither column is the safe one. They fail differently.

blocks.heading: One sentence worth keeping
text: Proof of stake does not remove the cost of agreement; it moves it from a bill you pay forever to a deposit you can lose once.
That is the end of how a chain agrees with itself. The rest of the course is about what people then built on top, and where it leaks.
